health_benefits: High-quality lean protein rich in niacin (B3), vitamin B6, and phosphorus; essential for muscle hypertrophy, metabolic rate, and cellular tissue repair.
intake_methods: Grilled, boiled, prepared in traditional South Indian chicken curry / pepper fry, or shredded into clear soups and salads.
Vitamin_Explanation: Skinless chicken breast is exceptionally dense in niacin (vitamin B3) and vitamin B6, vital for muscle metabolism.

health_benefits: Dense in bioavailable heme iron, zinc, and vitamin B12; prevents iron-deficiency anemia, supports red blood cell production, and builds stamina.
intake_methods: Stewed into mutton bone soup / leg soup (marakari), braised in mutton sukka with whole spices, or cooked in rich curries.
Vitamin_Explanation: Goat meat/mutton is an outstanding source of vitamin B12 and heme iron, essential for red blood cell formation.

health_benefits: Excellent source of marine Omega-3 fatty acids (EPA/DHA) and high-density protein; reduces arterial inflammation, supports brain function, and promotes cardiovascular wellness.
intake_methods: Tawa grilled/pan-seared with turmeric and chilli paste, simmered in traditional meen kulambu, or steamed with herbs.
Vitamin_Explanation: Vanjaram seer fish is extraordinarily rich in vitamin B12 and long-chain Omega-3s (EPA/DHA) for cognitive and cardiovascular wellness.

health_benefits: Extremely lean, low-calorie white fish packed with selenium and potassium; boosts metabolic health, protects thyroid function, and supports lean muscle recovery.
intake_methods: Cooked in sour and spicy village-style fish gravy (Sankara meen kulambu), baked with garlic-lemon marinade, or shallow fried.
Vitamin_Explanation: Red Snapper (Sankara) provides high-quality protein and vitamin B12 to support neurological health.

health_benefits: Eaten whole with bones; extraordinarily high in calcium and phosphorus to dramatically increase bone mineral density and prevent joint degradation.
intake_methods: Prepared as spicy Nethili meen fry, slow-cooked in tangy tomato-tamarind gravy, or dried and used in herbal thuvaiyals.
Vitamin_Explanation: Nethili anchovies supply remarkable concentrations of niacin (vitamin B3) and vitamin D alongside bioavailable calcium.

health_benefits: Powerhouse of long-chain Omega-3 fatty acids, vitamin D, and CoQ10; lowers blood triglycerides, improves insulin sensitivity, and protects brain neural health.
intake_methods: Cooked in spicy clay-pot Mathi kulambu with garlic and fenugreek seeds, grilled whole, or pan-fried with curry leaves.
Vitamin_Explanation: Mathi sardines are one of the few potent natural food sources of vitamin D and vitamin B12, critical for bone and immune health.

health_benefits: Delicate, easily digestible protein packed with vitamin B12 and healthy unsaturated fatty acids; aids eyesight health, rejuvenates skin, and supports cardiac flow.
intake_methods: Whole marinated tawa roast, cooked in coconut-coriander based fish curry, or gently steamed with ginger and pepper.
Vitamin_Explanation: White Pomfret supplies easily digestible protein, vitamin B12, and vitamin A for visual acuity and tissue repair.

health_benefits: Lean source of high-biological value protein, astaxanthin antioxidant, iodine, and selenium; aids thyroid regulation and cellular cellular defense.
intake_methods: Cooked into spicy Eral masala / thokku, simmered in coconut milk prawn curry, or pan-seared with crushed black pepper and garlic.
Vitamin_Explanation: Prawns provide vitamin B12, selenium, and astaxanthin antioxidant to support cellular metabolic defense.

health_benefits: Unrivaled concentration of bioavailable heme iron and complete protein; rapidly elevates blood hemoglobin levels, restores vitality, and combats severe anemia.
intake_methods: Scrambled into traditional South Indian Ratha Poriyal with shallots, green chillies, curry leaves, and grated coconut.
Vitamin_Explanation: Goat blood provides an exceptionally high concentration of vitamin B12 and bioavailable heme iron, crucial for rapid hemoglobin recovery.
